source: Financial Order of Operations ladder as specified in SPEC.md Section 13. Framework popularised by The Money Guy Show.
note: Thresholds live here, not in engine code, so tuning the ladder is a data edit. Evaluation is a sequential boolean gate: the first unmet step is the user's placement.

ladder.label: Cover basic living expenses + enrol in employer benefits
Starter emergency fund (~$1,000 or 1 month of expenses)
Build the full emergency fund (3–6 months)
Max a Roth IRA (or backdoor Roth)
Prepay low-interest debt or fund other goals

outOfBoundsFlags.label: Emergency fund sitting alongside high-interest debt
outOfBoundsFlags.guidance: Cash earning near nothing while a balance compounds above 7.5% is a losing trade. Keep the starter fund; send the rest at the debt.

outOfBoundsFlags.label: Not capturing the full employer match
outOfBoundsFlags.guidance: This is the only guaranteed return in the whole ladder. Contributing up to the cap comes before almost everything else.

outOfBoundsFlags.label: Debt-to-income above 36%
outOfBoundsFlags.guidance: Above the range most lenders treat as comfortable. It does not mean anything is wrong today — it does narrow your options.

outOfBoundsFlags.label: Savings rate below the 10–15% benchmark
outOfBoundsFlags.guidance: Below the range typically used as a floor. Worth checking against your expenses before treating it as a fact.

outOfBoundsFlags.label: High revolving balance relative to total debt
outOfBoundsFlags.guidance: A large share of your debt is revolving credit, which usually carries the highest rate and the most volatile minimum payment.
